rv.q: The revival by Hive North acknowledges the progress made in the intervening years as a result of the work of, and pressure from, activists and so provides hope in these increasingly dark times whilst also featuring an outstanding performance from Gabriel Clark.
The Night Larry Kramer Kissed Me, while showing its age, is a stark and upbeat reminder of how far we have come.
Gabriel Clark is utterly captivating from start to finish. Holding the stage alone for 75 minutes without a single dip in energy or focus, he commands the room with remarkable ease.

The work stands as a landmark in LGBTQ+ theatre, offering a deeply personal yet politically charged narrative that conveys the urgency of the early AIDS crisis while exploring enduring themes of community, love, and resistance that continue to resonate.

cn.t: Critics praise this fierce and deeply moving solo show, celebrating Gabriel Clark's performance in David Drake's honest, emotionally raw exploration of coming of age during the AIDS crisis, blending storytelling with humor and poignancy.
